name: Stop-motion object / tabletop macro
look: real-feeling tabletop objects shot at 12 fps, hands in shot, found materials.

fits.notes: hardware, creative tools, food, "handmade" brands. Needs a believable real-world set; faux versions fail if lighting is flat

products: flat lighting that exposes the fake

when_not: Avoid for flat lighting that exposes the fake.

type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text.

colour.guidance: hand-cut or label-maker type; kraft, felt, primary-coloured props.
colour.rule: Style palette fills the world; the brand colour takes the role named in brand_lock.colour_role and never drops below the contrast of the brand's own palette.

keeps: real product UI capture (composited as a screen plate, never redrawn)
brand_lock.colour_role: brand colour is one prop colour (kraft, felt and primary props otherwise)
brand_lock.type_role: hand-cut or label-maker type; brand face for the claim on a card prop
brand_lock.world_changes: tabletop set, objects hop on twos, hands in shot
brand_lock.rule: Under a brand lock the brand colour, type and logo stay; the style world (material, picture language, motion grammar, finish, sound) is what varies between looks. A branded launch shows 3 different style worlds.

hints: cardboard/foam-core sets, objects hop on 2s, hand-held light flicker, macro DOF
motion_grammar.note: grammars lists existing library/grammars ids; grammars_planned lists world grammars the engine plan adds (game-world, tabletop, os-desktop, type-only, editorial, collage, cinematic-world).

effects_note: rasan-fx passes (runtime/rasan-fx.js); order is the pass order. {brand_colour} / {second_ink} are filled from the brand or look palette.

codex_assets.prompt_template: tabletop photo-real {object} plate on kraft / felt background, soft directional shadow, found-object look, 3 variants for 12 fps boil
codex_assets.r1_note: tabletop photo-real object plates and background boards; the "found-object" look.
codex_assets.rules: Flat, evenly lit plain background (chroma green or pure white) for clean cut-outs; one prompt family with the same seed words; generate at 2x and downscale; never ask Codex for readable UI text or logos (typeset them in HTML).

build.recipe: `motion/stop-motion/stop-motion-laika-replacement.md`; Three.js physical scene with fixed-fps stepping, shadow-heavy lighting; or A1 + A2 with Codex plates.

product_ui_rule: If the film shows RasanAI Studio, use the current dark sidebar UI with the Describe...Final dot stepper (docs/brand/studio-ui/), as a real capture composited INTO this style; never the retired light UI.

palettes.name: Workbench
palettes.words: plywood table, dark walnut, tomato red felt, teal cardboard

palettes.name: Cardboard city
palettes.words: corrugated card, brown ink, mustard, denim blue

brand_lock.rule: Brand colour is the hero prop's felt or paint (the character, the box); table, cardboard and ink stay style-fixed. Slots marked brand take the brand colour (exact hex); slots marked style keep the palette value; brand-or-style takes the brand colour only when its contrast against the other slot is at least 4.5:1, else the palette value.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

pairings.note: Label-maker or typewriter tape labels stuck on objects; or letters cut from card.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

type.load: In a HyperFrames composition add the two <link> tags from `google` to <head> (plus rel=preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com), set font-family from `css`, and wait for document.fonts.ready before the first screenshot / timeline build. Offline renders: download the families once (they are OFL) into the project's fonts/ folder and use @font-face. The brand face always sets the real claim line and the product UI text; the style pairing is for the world's chrome and display.
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text. Under a brand lock keep the brand face for the claim and use the pairing's display for labels only.

passes.role: film grain for the macro look

finish.how: Runtime: RasanFX.create({ source, passes: [...] }) from runtime/rasan-fx.js, applied in the listed order, on the whole composition canvas or on the Codex plate only (plate-only when the type must stay crisp). `css` lists the cheap approximation kinds story boards and style frames draw with plain CSS (grain:<opacity>, scan:<opacity>, halftone, pixel, led-dots ...).

composition.grid: tabletop 3/4 view of a handmade set; props on cardboard risers; characters at the thirds
composition.fill: props fill 50%; the table is part of the world
composition.product_ui: UI is a printed paper screen or a real small monitor on the set, held at an angle

codex.template: {subject} {action}, {setting}. Camera and lens: 60 mm macro on a tabletop rig, f/4, shallow depth of field with a tilt-shift look, locked off. Lighting: a warm tungsten key from upper left, a small cool fill, soft contact shadows on the table. Material: felt, cardboard, painted wood, thumbtacks, masking tape, visible glue and fingerprints. Colour, locked to the palette {palette_words}, and nothing outside it. Texture and finish: fibre and fuzz on felt, paper grain, slight flicker between frames (hold on 2s or 3s). Avoid: no text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no smooth CG surfaces, no perfect symmetry, no clean vector, no glossy plastic, no floating objects without a rig, no text.
codex.camera: 60 mm macro on a tabletop rig, f/4, shallow depth of field with a tilt-shift look, locked off
codex.lighting: a warm tungsten key from upper left, a small cool fill, soft contact shadows on the table
codex.material: felt, cardboard, painted wood, thumbtacks, masking tape, visible glue and fingerprints
codex.colour_rule: Name the palette's colours in words (the palette's `words`), never hex codes; add 'and nothing outside this palette'. Pick one palette per film and keep it.
codex.texture: fibre and fuzz on felt, paper grain, slight flicker between frames (hold on 2s or 3s)
negatives: no floating objects without a rig

aspect.note: Plates: ask for about 12% bleed around the frame so the camera can travel; keep the calm side empty for type. Generate 16:9 for the frame, 1:1 for sprite sheets and objects.

consistency.anchor: Make the anchor plate first, approve it by eye, then pass it as --ref to every other image (imagegen batch does this with --world).
consistency.style_line: Append the world bible's style line (30-45 words, no hex) to every prompt.
consistency.seed_words: Keep these words verbatim in every prompt of the film: felt; 60 mm macro on a tabletop rig; plywood table, dark walnut, tomato red felt, teal cardboard.

sprite_sheet.rules: Not a sprite style. For a cut-out object or character use --transparent (flat #00FF00 key, then despill); one subject, no shadow plane.

do: Animate on 2s or 3s: pops, not tweens
Show the maker's marks: glue, tape, fingerprints
Use real macro depth of field
cheap_ways: Wool texture filter on a render
Smooth 60 fps motion that is not stop-motion
Perfectly clean cardboard with no glue or tape
